arxiv-2103-00146.title: From distributive ℓ \ell -monoids to ℓ \ell -groups, and back again
arxiv-2103-00146.creator: Almudena Colacito, Nikolaos Galatos, George Metcalfe, Simon Santschi
arxiv-2103-00146.description: Abstract We prove that an inverse-free equation is valid in the variety 𝖫𝖦 \mathsf{LG} of lattice-ordered groups ( ℓ \ell -groups) if and only if it is valid in the variety 𝖣𝖫𝖬 \mathsf{DLM} of distributive lattice-ordered monoids (distributive ℓ \ell -monoids).

arxiv-2201-04103.title: Sylow-conjugate number fields
arxiv-2201-04103.creator: Alexander Lubotzky, Danny Neftin
arxiv-2201-04103.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Alexander Lubotzky, Danny Neftin. By a classical result of Neukirch and Uchida, a number field K K is determined by the structure of its absolute Galois group Gal ⁡ ( K ) \Gal(K) . We show that K K is not determined by the structure of the Sylow subgroups of Gal ⁡ ( K ) \Gal(K) , answering a question raised by Florian Pop.

arxiv-2210-08750.title: Keep Me Updated! Memory Management in Long-term Conversations
arxiv-2210-08750.creator: Sanghwan Bae Donghyun Kwak Soyoung Kang Min Young Lee, Sungdong Kim Yuin Jeong Hyeri Kim Sang-Woo Lee, Woomyoung Park Nako Sung, NAVER CLOVA NAVER AI Lab KAIST AI
arxiv-2210-08750.description: Abstract Remembering important information from the past and continuing to talk about it in the present are crucial in long-term conversations. However, previous literature does not deal with cases where the memorized information is outdated, which may cause confusion in later conversations.

arxiv-2309-11856.title: Activation Compression of Graph Neural Networks using Block-wise Quantization with Improved Variance Minimization
arxiv-2309-11856.creator: Sebastian Eliassen, Raghavendra Selvan \sthanks The authors acknowledge funding received under European Union’s Horizon Europe Research and Innovation programme under grant agreements No. 101070284 and No. 101070408
arxiv-2309-11856.description: Abstract Efficient training of large-scale graph neural networks (GNNs) has been studied with a specific focus on reducing their memory consumption. Work by Liu et al. (2022) proposed extreme activation compression (EXACT) which demonstrated drastic reduction in memory consumption by performing quantization of the intermediate activation maps down to using INT2 precision.

arxiv-2310-20528.title: Higher-order reductions of the Mikhalev system
arxiv-2310-20528.creator: E.V. Ferapontov 1,2 , V.S. Novikov 1 , I. Roustemoglou 1
arxiv-2310-20528.description: Abstract 1 Department of Mathematical Sciences, Loughborough University Loughborough, Leicestershire LE11 3TU, United Kingdom 2 Institute of Mathematics, Ufa Federal Research Centre Russian Academy of Sciences 112 Chernyshevsky Street, Ufa 450077, Russia e-mails: E.V.Ferapontov@lboro.ac.uk V.Novikov@lboro.ac.uk I.Roustemoglou@lboro.ac.uk We consider the 3D Mikhalev system, u_{t}=w_{x},\quad u_{y}=w_{t}-uw_{x}+wu_{x}, which has first appeared in the context of KdV-type hierarchies.

arxiv-2311-02936.title: Magnetic moments of decuplet baryons in asymmetric strange hadronic matter at finite temperature
arxiv-2311-02936.creator: Arvind Kumar, Suneel Dutt, Harleen Dahiya
arxiv-2311-02936.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Arvind Kumar, Suneel Dutt, Harleen Dahiya. In the present work we study the masses and magnetic moments of decuplet baryons in isospin asymmetric strange hadronic medium at finite temperature using chiral SU(3) quark mean field model. In the strange isospin asymmetric medium, the properties of baryons in chiral SU(3) mean field model are modified through the exchange of scalar fields σ \sigma , ζ \zeta and δ \delta and the vector fields ω \omega , ρ \rho and ϕ \phi .

arxiv-2410-23005.title: Improving Musical Accompaniment Co-creation via Diffusion Transformers
arxiv-2410-23005.creator: Javier Nistal, Marco Pasini, Stefan Lattner
arxiv-2410-23005.description: Abstract Building upon Diff-A-Riff, a latent diffusion model for musical instrument accompaniment generation, we present a series of improvements targeting quality, diversity, inference speed, and text-driven control. First, we upgrade the underlying autoencoder to a stereo-capable model with superior fidelity and replace the latent U-Net with a Diffusion Transformer.

This research work is also supported in part by NSERC-DG RGPIN-2020-04759 and Fonds
arxiv-2512-06133.creator: Nyoba Tchonkeu, Melone, Berkane, Soulaimane, Hamel, Tarek
arxiv-2512-06133.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Nyoba Tchonkeu, Melone, Berkane, Soulaimane, Hamel, Tarek. This paper addresses the problem of estimating air velocity and full attitude for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in GNSS-denied environments using minimal onboard sensing—an interesting and practically relevant challenge for UAV navigation.

arxiv-2602-15546.title: CEPAE: Conditional Entropy-Penalized Autoencoders for Time Series Counterfactuals
arxiv-2602-15546.creator: Tomàs Garriga tomas.garriga_dicuzzo@novartis.com, Gerard Sanz gerard.sanz_estape@novartis.com, Eduard Serrahima de Cambra eduard.serrahima_de_cambra@novartis.com, Axel Brando axel.brando@bsc.es
arxiv-2602-15546.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Tomàs Garriga tomas.garriga_dicuzzo@novartis.com, Gerard Sanz gerard.sanz_estape@novartis.com, Eduard Serrahima de Cambra eduard.serrahima_de_cambra@novartis.com, Axel Brando axel.brando@bsc.es. The ability to accurately perform counterfactual inference on time series is crucial for decision-making in fields like finance, healthcare, and marketing, as it allows us to understand the impact of events or treatments on outcomes over time. In this paper, we introduce a new counterfactual inference approach tailored to time series data impacted by market events, which is motivated by an industrial application.

pmc-11285467.title: Perceptions, experiences, and motivation of COVID-19 vaccine trial participants in South Africa: a qualitative study
pmc-11285467.creator: Thandeka Nkosi, Chanelle Mulopo, Bey-Marrié Schmidt
pmc-11285467.description: BackgroundThe informed consent process is an important step in conducting ethical clinical trials, as it ensures that research participants are aware of their rights and responsibilities in clinical trials. This study explored participants’ perceptions, experiences and the factors motivating their participation in a COVID-19 vaccine trial in South Africa.

pmc-11863083.title: Identifying Depression Subtypes and Investigating their Consistency and Transitions in a 1-Year Cohort Analysis
pmc-11863083.creator: C Oetzmann, N Cummins, F Lamers, F Matcham, K M White, J M Haro, S Siddi, S Vairavan, B W Penninx, V A Narayan, M Hotopf, E Carr
pmc-11863083.description: Introduction Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is a complex mental health condition characterized by a wide spectrum of symptoms. According to the Diagnostic Statistical Manual 5 (DSM-5) criteria, patients can present with up to 1,497 different symptom combinations, yet all receive the same MDD diagnosis.

pmc-12400573.title: U-FISH: a fluorescent spot detector for imaging-based spatial-omics analysis and AI-assisted FISH diagnosis
pmc-12400573.creator: Weize Xu, Huaiyuan Cai, Qian Zhang, Zhengze Wang, Jiajun Yang, Xiaofeng Wu, Chengwen Li, Chenghua Cui, Changzhi Liu, Jin He, Florian Mueller, Jinxia Dai, Chen Hao, Wei Ouyang, Gang Cao
pmc-12400573.description: Imaging-based spatial-omics advances biomedical discoveries with subcellular resolution and high sensitivity, but accurately identifying signal spots from diverse images remains challenging. We develop U-FISH, a deep learning method that enhances images for consistent spot detection across various spatial-omics data. We establish a comprehensive FISH image dataset from seven spatial-omics methods.

pmc-12538739.title: Bridging metabolism and immuno-inflammation: a novel framework to characterize dilated cardiomyopathy subtype
pmc-12538739.creator: Cheng Yu, Changhu Liu, Bingjun Liu, Jiaying Feng, Yichen Deng, Jing Yuan
pmc-12538739.description: BackgroundThe heterogeneous subtypes in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) are poorly characterized, thus posing challenges to risk stratification. This study aimed to establish a DCM subtype framework based on metabolic and immunoinflammatory factors.MethodsDCM subtypes were identified using unsupervised clustering based on the expression patterns of metabolism-related genes in the left ventricular myocardium of 89 DCM patients.

pmc-12607808.title: New-Onset Graves’ Ophthalmopathy After Treatment with Pembrolizumab: A Case Report and a Review of the Literature
pmc-12607808.creator: Moduo Pan, Xuecong Zhou, Yuan Wu
pmc-12607808.description: Background and Clinical Significance: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), a revolutionary class of oncology therapeutics that enhance T cell-mediated antitumor immunity, are associated with various immune-related adverse events (IRAEs). While destructive thyroiditis and hypothyroidism are common, ICI-induced Graves’ disease (GD) is exceedingly rare, and the occurrence of concomitant Graves’ ophthalmopathy (GO) is even rarer.

pmc-13042282.title: Overall coronary disease burden modifies the prognostic benefit of CTO-PCI: a SYNTAX score–stratified meta-analysis
pmc-13042282.creator: Nino Cocco, Kambis Mashayekhi, Agostino Spanò, Michael Behnes, Pierfrancesco Agostoni, Daniel Weilenmann, Claudiu Ungureanu, Giuseppe Colletti, Maourane Boukhris, Giulio Cocco, Cammalleri Valeria, Annunziata Nusca, Gian Paolo Ussia, Gregor Leibundgut
pmc-13042282.description: AimsExtensive coronary artery disease (CAD) coexisting with chronic total occlusion (CTO) is associated with adverse outcomes, yet patients with advanced CAD are often underrepresented in randomized trials, and the prognostic impact of CTO percutaneous coronary intervention (CTO-PCI) across different levels of anatomical complexity remains uncertain.

pmc-13073277.title: Transcriptomic Profiling Identifies TALAM1 and LINC00702 as HIV-1-Responsive lncRNAs in Microglia
pmc-13073277.creator: Victoria Rojas-Celis, Catalina Millan-Hidalgo, Izabela Mamede, Isidora Morales-Vejar, Isidora Pittet-Díaz, Diego Fernández-Rodríguez, Paulo P. Amaral, Helder I. Nakaya, Sebastián Reyes-Cerpa, Fernando Valiente-Echeverría, Camila Pereira-Montecinos, Daniela Toro-Ascuy
pmc-13073277.description: Microglia, the resident macrophages of the central nervous system (CNS), serve as the primary reservoir of HIV-1 in the brain and play a crucial role in the development of HIV-1-associated neurocognitive disorders (HAND). While long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) have emerged as essential regulators of HIV-1 replication in T cells and macrophages, their role in microglia remains poorly understood.

pmc-13393036.title: Terbium(III)-Doped Silica Surface of Fe(II) Spin Crossover Nanoparticles as a Multifunctional Interface
pmc-13393036.creator: Nikolia Lalioti, Maria Katsikini, Fani Pinakidou, Labrini Sygellou, Kyriacos Georgiou, Sotirios Christodoulou, Francesco D’Acapito, Radim Mach, Ondrej Malina, Vassilis Tangoulis
pmc-13393036.description: Spin-crossover (SCO) nanoparticles (NPs) of the ID coordination polymer [Fe­(HTrz)2(Trz)]·(BF4), where HTrz = 1H-1,2,4-triazole, have been synthesized with integrated luminescence properties, focusing on the role of dopant trivalent Terbium (Tb) ions. Using a reverse micelle method, three types of nanoparticles were synthesized: pristine NPs (NP1), silica covered (NP2), and Tb-doped (NP3) NPs.

pmc-13394705.title: From community engagement to lived experience leadership: a systematic review of HIV services among men who have sex with men
pmc-13394705.creator: Aron Harold G Pamoso, Elizabeth Waldron, I Nyoman Sutarsa, Mary Lou Rasmussen, Brett Scholz
pmc-13394705.description: Community responses are essential to achieving the global goal of Ending AIDS by 2030, yet men who have sex with men (MSM) remain underrepresented and often tokenized within HIV initiatives. While community engagement is widely emphasized, far less attention has been given to leadership rooted in lived experience.

pmc-13633459.title: Molecular Characterization of Cocarriage Carbapenemase Genes in Clinical Pseudomonas aeruginosa
pmc-13633459.creator: Pompy Dey, Sudip Kumar Chowdhury, Ayesha Ahmed Khan, Md Fourkan Uddin, Swagata Nandy, Shawon Banerjee, Puja Mitra, Kathirvel Maruthai
pmc-13633459.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a major nosocomial pathogen associated with multidrug resistance and limited treatment options. Carbapenem resistance mediated by carbapenemase genes is an increasing threat, yet molecular epidemiological data from Bangladesh remain scarce.ObjectivesTo determine the prevalence of carbapenem resistance and carbapenemase genes, characterize cocarriage of carbapenemase determinants, evaluate phenotypic and molecular detection methods, and identify factors associated with carbapenem‐resistant P. aeruginosa.MethodsA cross‐sectional study was conducted from January to December 2023 at a tertiary‐care teaching hospital in Chattogram, Bangladesh.

pmc-13634573.title: Suppressing Photothermal Artifacts in Flexible Fluorescent Fiber‐Optic Sensors for Accurate and Precise In Situ Temperature Monitoring
pmc-13634573.creator: Sijie Su, Jinjian Yu, Pengyuan Dong, Xin Wang, Jing Lyu, Jiulin Gan, Enhai Song, Qinyuan Zhang
pmc-13634573.description: Ratiometric flexible fluorescent fiber‐optic sensors, featuring self‐calibration and precise spatial localization, are emerging as a robust platform for in situ thermal monitoring, advancing applications such as battery safety management and biomedical diagnostics. However, measurement artifacts induced by the inherent photothermal effect remain largely overlooked, posing a challenge to high‐accuracy temperature sensing.
